'''Edgar Y. Choueiri''' (born 1961 in Lebanon) is a Lebanese American plasma [[physicist]] and previously president of the [[Lebanese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>Press Reference (Daily Princetonian): [https://www.princeton.edu/main/news/archive/S22/45/18G22/index.xml?section=science "ASL President Elected"]</ref> He is best known for clarifying the role of [[plasma instabilities]] in spacecraft electric thrusters (see [[plasma propulsion]]), for conceiving and developing new [[spacecraft propulsion]] concepts and, more recently, for his work on [[3D audio]].<ref>[https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2013/01/28/music-to-your-ears; Music to your Ears] by Adam Gopnik in the New Yorker, 20 January 2013</ref><ref>[https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2011/01/what-perfection-sounds-like/8377/;title "What Perfection Sounds Like"], ''The Atlantic'', March 2011</ref><ref>[https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2011/02/notes-on-the-search-for-startling-innovations-in-3d-audio/71010/;title "Notes on the Search for Startling Innovations in 3D Audio"], ''The Atlantic'', 10 February 2011</ref>

== Career ==
Choueiri is professor of applied physics and aerospace engineering at [[Princeton University]]. At Princeton, he also serves as director of the electric propulsion and plasma dynamics laboratory, director of Princeton's engineering physics program, and the principal investigator of Princeton University's 3D audio and applied acoustics lab (3D3A). He is Fellow of the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] (AIAA) and previously president of the [[Electric Rocket Propulsion Society]].

In 2004, Choueiri was knighted (Medal of the [[Order of the Cedars]], Rank of Knight) for his work in astronautics by the president of the [[Republic of Lebanon]].<ref>Press Reference (Daily Princetonian): [http://www.dailyprincetonian.com/2004/11/08/11345 Choueiri in Lebanon] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110302231848/http://www.dailyprincetonian.com/2004/11/08/11345/ |date=2 March 2011 }}</ref>
